queries: large language models alone general intelligence limitations proof language alone

sources_considered.why: Primary research describing broad GPT-4 capabilities and explicitly incomplete AGI; relevant counterpressure but not a decisive LLM-only demonstration.
A formal limitations argument, but its prompt-channel assumptions and universal problem-solving target are narrower and different from the claim's ordinary meaning.
Recent controlled research distinguishes language models from the software surrounding them.
A secondary overview surfaced in search. Primary research was preferred.

evidence_items.explanation: The researchers report capabilities across several domains and characterize their early GPT-4 as incomplete AGI. This challenges dismissive readings of LLM capability, but does not establish the independently validated, language-only general intelligence required for contradiction.

The paper derives limitations under restrictions on communicated task information and admissible outputs. Failure to solve arbitrary tasks under those assumptions does not establish inability to achieve human-level general intelligence.

receipt.public_excerpt: Yet language models rarely act alone.

evidence_items.explanation: This study evaluates models constructing and revising surrounding software on interactive games. Its results concern combined systems and a bounded evaluation, so neither success nor failure settles the LLM-only assertion.

unresolved_gaps: No retrieved source demonstrates independently validated human-level general intelligence from a language-only LLM alone.
No retrieved impossibility result covers the full claim under its ordinary reading.
Marcus supplies neither a capability threshold nor a precise boundary for what counts as an LLM alone.
